prompt: Put the three steps of SwiftUI layout in order.
hint: Offer, decide, place.
items: The child chooses its size and reports it

prompt: A `Text("50 min")` is offered the full width of a 390-point screen. How wide does it end up?
hint: Filling space is something a view chooses.

choices.text: 390 points, since the parent set it
choices.why: A parent offers; it does not set.

choices.text: The width of its words
choices.why: Right: text takes what its words need and no more.

choices.text: Half the screen, the default for text
choices.why: There is no such default.

choices.text: Zero until a frame is given
choices.why: A text has an ideal size of its own.

prompt: Which of these views fills whatever space it is offered?
hint: A shape always occupies the space offered.

choices.text: `Text("SQL Databases")`
choices.why: Text takes its words' width.

choices.text: `Image(systemName: "checkmark")` at its natural size
choices.why: An image at its natural size keeps that size.

choices.text: `Ellipse()`
choices.why: Right: the documentation's own example of a shape filling the offer.

choices.text: An `HStack` of two texts with no spacer
choices.why: It is as wide as its children's ideal widths.

prompt: In the course row, what does `VStack(alignment: .leading)` do?
hint: A VStack aligns on the other axis.

choices.text: Aligns the two texts' leading edges
choices.why: Right: without it they would be centred on each other.

choices.text: Puts the stack on the left of the screen
choices.why: It aligns the children inside the stack, not the stack in the row.

choices.text: Makes the text read right to left
choices.why: Leading follows the language's direction; it does not change it.

choices.text: Stacks the title and caption side by side
choices.why: A VStack stacks vertically whatever its alignment.

prompt: According to Apple's documentation, what is the difference between `HStack` and `LazyHStack`?
hint: One creates its children only when needed.

choices.text: A `LazyHStack` cannot hold more than ten children
choices.why: There is no such limit; lazy containers exist for long content.

choices.text: An `HStack` lays out right to left
choices.why: Both follow the layout direction.

choices.text: `HStack` creates every child at once
choices.why: Right; `LazyHStack` creates them as they are needed.

choices.text: `LazyHStack` ignores spacing
choices.why: It takes a spacing like any stack.

prompt: `Text("50 min").frame(width: 200).border(.red)`. What is 200 points wide?
hint: Two views, two sizes.

choices.text: The text, which the frame stretched
choices.why: The frame proposes 200; the text still chooses its words' width.

choices.text: The frame, with the red border around it
choices.why: Right: the text sits in the middle of it.

choices.text: Both, since a frame sets the size
choices.why: A frame is a new view around the old one.

choices.text: Neither: the border adds its own width
choices.why: The border is drawn on the frame's edge.

prompt: What does `.frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading)` do to a heading in a `VStack`?
hint: A frame that accepts any width.

choices.text: Makes the font as large as the screen allows
choices.why: A frame has nothing to do with the font.

choices.text: Wraps the text onto as many lines as it has words
choices.why: A wide frame gives the text more room, not less.

choices.text: Takes the full width and puts the text at its left
choices.why: Right: the usual way to left-align a heading across the screen.

choices.text: Nothing, since `.infinity` is not a size
choices.why: It is a maximum: the frame accepts any width offered.

prompt: A short status label truncates to `Do…` in a narrow row. Which modifier stops it from being cut, and what is the risk?
hint: It makes the view take its ideal size.

choices.text: `.fixedSize()`; long text runs off screen
choices.why: Right: it ignores the proposal, which is fine for a short label.

choices.text: `.frame(width: 0)`; the label disappears from the row
choices.why: A zero-width frame proposes zero, the opposite.

choices.text: `.padding()`; the row grows taller than its neighbours
choices.why: Padding takes space away from the text.

choices.text: `.border(.red)`; the border hides the end
choices.why: A border changes no size.

prompt: In the course row, why align the `HStack` on `.firstTextBaseline` rather than `.center`?
hint: Where do the minutes sit with each?

choices.text: `.center` is not allowed in an `HStack`
choices.why: It is the default.

choices.text: Baselines make the row shorter
choices.why: Alignment moves views; it is not about height.

choices.text: So the minutes share a line with the title
choices.why: Right: centred, they sit between title and caption.

choices.text: So the caption moves to the right of the minutes
choices.why: Alignment does not reorder the children.

prompt: The line letters sit on, which `.firstTextBaseline` lines up across texts of different sizes, is the ___.
hint: Printers have used the word for centuries.

prompt: Where does a badge in `ZStack(alignment: .topTrailing)` sit relative to the icon under it?
hint: Top, and the trailing side.

choices.text: Centred on the icon
choices.why: That is `.center`.

choices.text: Below the icon
choices.why: A ZStack layers; it does not stack downwards.

choices.text: Top-right corner
choices.why: Right: top and trailing.

choices.text: Behind the icon
choices.why: Later layers are in front.

prompt: `HStack { Text("SQL Databases"); Text("50 min") }` sits in a list row. Without a `Spacer`, how wide is the stack?
hint: The sentence about stacks with no spacer.

choices.text: The width of the row
choices.why: A stack fills the row only if something in it wants to.

choices.text: Its children's ideal widths, plus spacing
choices.why: Right, as Apple's documentation for `Spacer` says.

choices.text: Zero, until the list gives the stack a width of its own
choices.why: Children have ideal widths of their own.

choices.text: Half the row, one half per text
choices.why: Nothing splits the row into halves.

prompt: `WeekView().background(.thinMaterial, in: RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 12)).padding()`: what does this order draw?
hint: Each modifier wraps everything before it.

choices.text: The same as with `.padding()` first
choices.why: Section 06 says the order matters, and lesson 5 starts with it.

choices.text: A tight background, space outside it
choices.why: Right: the padding wraps the background, so it adds space outside.

choices.text: A background with room inside around the content
choices.why: That is the other order, padding then background.

choices.text: No background, since padding hides it
choices.why: Padding draws nothing.

prompt: Why does the progress bar in section 07 have `.frame(height: 8)` outside the `GeometryReader`?
hint: What does a reader do with the space it is offered?

choices.text: To make the capsule's corners round at both ends
choices.why: A capsule is round already.

choices.text: The reader takes all the height offered
choices.why: Right: without the frame it would push the rest off the screen.

choices.text: So `proxy.size.width` is not zero
choices.why: The width comes from the parent's proposal, not from the height.

choices.text: To divide by one in an empty week
choices.why: That is what `max(total.planned, 1)` is for.

prompt: Match each need to the tool section 07 recommends.
hint: Three newer tools and the old one.

pairs.left: A width that is a fraction of the screen
The largest of several layouts that fits
Drawing from the offered size itself

prompt: In the first row `layout.swift` printed, how wide was the `Spacer`?
hint: The middle line of the first block.

prompt: In the second row, how many points did `Mobile Fundamentals` get, against an ideal of 150?
hint: It was served last.

prompt: In the model, why is `40 min` served before `Mobile Fundamentals` although it is written after it?
hint: Service order is not position.

choices.text: Because the stack serves children from right to left
choices.why: The icon on the far left was served first.

choices.text: It is less flexible: its ideal width is smaller
choices.why: Right: a label's flexibility is its ideal width, 48 against 150.

choices.text: Because numbers are measured before words
choices.why: The model knows nothing of numbers; it compares flexibility.

choices.text: Because it is shorter to type
choices.why: Its ideal width matters, not its spelling.

prompt: Which statement about `layout.swift` is true?
hint: Read the section's own warning.

choices.text: It is SwiftUI's `HStack` compiled for Linux
choices.why: SwiftUI has no Linux version; this is a model written for the course.

choices.text: Its widths match what an iPhone draws, to the point
choices.why: The label widths are chosen numbers, and the model leaves rules out.

choices.text: It leaves layout priority out of the model
choices.why: Right, along with minimum lengths and heights.

choices.text: It needs a Mac, because `padding(toLength:)` is Apple-only
choices.why: It ran on Linux; Foundation has that method there.

prompt: Match each child type in `layout.swift` to the SwiftUI view it stands for.
hint: The comments above each type.

prompt: A row is `HStack { Text(title); Text(minutes).frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .trailing) }` with no `Spacer`. Where do the minutes appear?
hint: A frame with an infinite maximum behaves like a spacer.

choices.text: At the right edge of the row
choices.why: Right: the frame takes what is left and puts the text at its trailing edge.

choices.text: Right after the title, since there is no spacer
choices.why: The flexible frame does the spacer's work.

choices.text: Centred in the row
choices.why: The alignment is `.trailing`.

choices.text: Under the title, on a new line
choices.why: An HStack never moves a child to a new line.

prompt: Which of these ran for this lesson? Choose all that apply.
hint: One program, and no SwiftUI.

choices.text: `swift layout.swift`
choices.why: Yes: section 08's capture.

choices.text: The `CourseRow` of section 03
choices.why: No: it imports SwiftUI.

choices.text: The progress bar's `GeometryReader`
choices.why: No: written from the documentation.

choices.text: A preview comparing the model with SwiftUI
choices.why: No: previews need Xcode on a Mac.
